fields.study_design: narrative literature review (no stated search method, databases or selection criteria; secondary sources on kiosks in Kenya, Malawi, Zambia, Mozambique, Nigeria, Uganda and others)
fields.population: urban poor in informal settlements of African cities (examples: Kisumu, Nairobi, Lilongwe, Blantyre, Lusaka, Maputo, Eldoret)
fields.sample_size: not stated: no search strategy, no count of reviewed studies (about 25 sources cited in the text)
fields.effect_measure: narrative synthesis under five headings (service management, reliability, pricing, water quality, consumer perception) quoting figures from the cited studies; no pooled estimate
fields.effect_estimate: Reported from cited studies (not appraised): a kiosk serves 500 to 3,000 people a day; in Kisumu kiosk operations were interrupted 3.3 hours a day by delayed supply and more than 80% of respondents found kiosks unreliable; in Lilongwe about half of 50 sampled kiosks were set to close because tariffs were unaffordable; water bought in bulk at Ksh 11/m3 was sold at Ksh 128/m3 in Kenyan settlements; kiosk water cost MZN 150 a month against MZN 20 for borehole water per household in Mozambique; household stored water was more contaminated than kiosk water in Malawi. Regulators set tariffs but allow operators leeway and enforce little; the authors recommend automation (water ATMs), tariff enforcement by regulators, storage reservoirs and hygiene education.
fields.section: Full text (4 pages): Introduction; contextual role of kiosks 2.1-2.5; Discussion and recommendations; Conclusion
fields.exact_location: Sections 2.1 (service management), 2.2 (reliability), 2.3 (pricing), 2.4 (quality), 2.5 (perceptions); Water Conservation and Management 9(2):335-338

evidence_level: Single-source evidence: a short narrative review of water kiosks for the urban poor in Africa, with no stated search or selection method, quoting figures from other studies; read in full text 2026-10-04.
pdf_note: Water Conservation & Management 9(2):335-338, English, 4 pages read in full (Drive file S320_Nyika_2025...pdf); the first-page header of the converted text carries the title of an unrelated paper (carbon dots from sawdust), a publisher layout error
notes: ELIGIBILITY FLAG: a narrative review with no stated method and no primary data; inclusion criterion 3 (empirical evidence or systematic empirical synthesis) is doubtful. Regulation of kiosk tariffs is the legal/administrative content. Candidate for the criterion-3 audit (A22).
